Vacancy: Community Sports Coordinator (Fixed-Term, 18 Months)

A  Northgate Borough Council is seeking an energetic Community Sports Coordinator to increase participation in sport and physical activity among young people aged 11 to 18, particularly in neighbourhoods where participation is currently low. The post is funded for eighteen months by a regional health grant, with the possibility of extension if further funding is secured.

B  Main responsibilities. You will organise weekly after-school sessions in partnership with schools and youth clubs, recruit and support a team of volunteer coaches, and plan two large sports festivals each year. You will also collect information on attendance and prepare quarterly reports for the funding body.

C  About you. You will have experience of working with young people in a sports, education or youth work setting, and you should hold at least one recognised coaching qualification. Excellent communication and organisational skills are essential. Because the role involves travelling between venues, a driving licence and access to a car are required; mileage expenses will be paid. Some evening and weekend work will be necessary, for which time off in lieu will be given.

D  How to apply. Download an application form from the council website and return it by email. CVs alone will not be accepted. The closing date is 14 May, and interviews will take place in the week beginning 26 May. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to lead a short practical activity with a group of young people as part of the interview.

The coordinator post could continue beyond eighteen months.
explanation: 第A段落にさらに資金が得られれば延長の可能性があるとあるので TRUE。

passage:
Safe Lifting at Work: Guidance for Warehouse Staff

A  Injuries caused by lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling loads are among the most common causes of time off work in warehouses. Many of these injuries affect the back and develop gradually rather than as the result of a single accident. This guidance explains how to reduce the risk. It does not replace the practical training that all new staff must complete before handling loads.

B  Before lifting, think about the task. Could a trolley, pallet truck or hoist be used instead? Is the load too heavy or awkward for one person? Check the route you will take and remove any obstacles. If the weight of a load is not marked, test it by rocking it gently from side to side before attempting to lift it.

C  When lifting, place your feet apart, with one leg slightly forward for balance. Bend your knees rather than your back, keep the load close to your waist and avoid twisting your body; turn by moving your feet instead. Lift smoothly without jerking, and if you cannot see over the load, do not carry it.

D  Team lifts must be planned. One person should be responsible for giving clear instructions, such as when to lift and when to put the load down. As a general guide, two people can safely lift about two thirds of the total that each could manage alone, not twice as much.

E  If you feel pain or discomfort, stop and report it to your supervisor as soon as possible. Early reporting allows problems to be investigated before they cause serious injury. All incidents, including near misses, must be recorded in the accident book kept in the supervisors' office.
question:
Does the following statement agree with the information given in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

explanation: 第A段落にこのガイドは実技研修の代わりにはならないとあるので FALSE。

passage:
Fire Safety Procedure: Lindqvist House Offices

A  If you discover a fire. Raise the alarm immediately by breaking the glass on the nearest red fire alarm point. Do not try to put out the fire unless it is very small and you have been trained to use a fire extinguisher.

B  When the alarm sounds. Leave the building by the nearest safe exit, closing doors behind you. Do not use the lifts and do not stop to collect personal belongings. Visitors should be accompanied by the member of staff they came to see.

C  Assembly point. Go to the assembly point in the car park opposite the main entrance and report to your floor's fire warden, who wears a yellow jacket. Do not leave the assembly point until you are told it is safe to do so, as wardens need to check that everyone is out of the building.

D  Staff who need help. If you have a disability or medical condition that would make it difficult to leave the building quickly, please speak to the facilities manager so that a personal evacuation plan can be prepared for you.

E  Fire drills. The alarm is tested every Wednesday at 10 a.m.; this test lasts less than a minute and you do not need to leave. A full evacuation drill takes place twice a year without advance warning.

passage:
Working Comfortably at a Computer

A  Many office employees spend most of their working day at a computer. Although this is not dangerous in the way that operating machinery can be, poor working habits can lead to aches and pains in the neck, shoulders, back and wrists, as well as tired eyes and headaches. Our company is required to assess every workstation, and you can request an assessment at any time by contacting the health and safety team.

B  Set up your chair so that your feet rest flat on the floor, or on a footrest if necessary, and your thighs are roughly horizontal. The backrest should support the lower part of your back. Your screen should be about an arm's length away, with the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level. If you use a laptop for long periods, connect it to a separate keyboard and mouse and raise the screen with a stand, which can be ordered free of charge from the facilities team.

C  Take regular short breaks or change to a different activity, such as making phone calls or filing, every hour or so. Short, frequent breaks are better than occasional long ones. To reduce eye strain, look away from the screen at a distant object from time to time and make sure that windows and lights do not cause glare on the screen.

D  Employees who use screens regularly as part of their job are entitled to an eye test paid for by the company. If the optician states that you need glasses specifically for screen work, the company will contribute towards the cost of a basic pair.

explanation: 第B段落にスタンドは無料で注文できるとあるので TRUE。

passage:
Working Comfortably at a Computer

A  Many office employees spend most of their working day at a computer. Although this is not dangerous in the way that operating machinery can be, poor working habits can lead to aches and pains in the neck, shoulders, back and wrists, as well as tired eyes and headaches. Our company is required to assess every workstation, and you can request an assessment at any time by contacting the health and safety team.

B  Set up your chair so that your feet rest flat on the floor, or on a footrest if necessary, and your thighs are roughly horizontal. The backrest should support the lower part of your back. Your screen should be about an arm's length away, with the top of the screen at or slightly below eye level. If you use a laptop for long periods, connect it to a separate keyboard and mouse and raise the screen with a stand, which can be ordered free of charge from the facilities team.

C  Take regular short breaks or change to a different activity, such as making phone calls or filing, every hour or so. Short, frequent breaks are better than occasional long ones. To reduce eye strain, look away from the screen at a distant object from time to time and make sure that windows and lights do not cause glare on the screen.

D  Employees who use screens regularly as part of their job are entitled to an eye test paid for by the company. If the optician states that you need glasses specifically for screen work, the company will contribute towards the cost of a basic pair.
question:
Complete the sentence below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for the answer.
The top of the screen should be at or slightly below ______.
explanation: 第B段落 "at or slightly below eye level" から。

Hillview Community Centre: Evening Classes, Autumn Term

E  Guitar Club. An informal group for people who already play a little and want to improve. We learn new songs together and occasionally perform at centre events. Bring your own guitar. Thursdays, 7.30–9 p.m.

F  Family History. Find out how to research your ancestors using online records, old newspapers and local archives. The course includes a visit to the county records office. Mondays, 7–9 p.m.

a class that new students can join after the term has started

passage:
Evening Classes: Enrolment, Fees and Refunds

A  Enrolment opens four weeks before the start of each term. You can enrol online, by telephone or in person at the reception desk. Places are allocated in the order in which bookings are received, and popular classes often fill within a few days, so early booking is recommended. If a class is full, you can add your name to a waiting list and we will contact you if a place becomes available.

B  Course fees must be paid in full at the time of enrolment. Reduced fees are available for people over 65, full-time students and those receiving certain state benefits; you will need to show proof of eligibility when you enrol. Some classes also charge a small materials fee, which is shown in the course description.

C  If you cancel your place at least seven days before the course begins, you will receive a full refund minus a £10 administration charge. We are unable to give refunds for cancellations made after this point, except in cases of serious illness supported by a medical certificate. If we cancel a class because too few people have enrolled, you will be offered a full refund or a place on another course.

D  Classes will not run during the half-term holiday or on public holidays. If a tutor is ill, we will try to arrange a replacement; if this is not possible, the session will be added at the end of the course. Students will be informed of any changes by text message.

Places on classes are given to students in the order that they book.
